सर्वत्र संपदस्तस्य संतुष्टं यस्य मानसम् ..
उपानद्गूढपादस्य ननु चर्मावृतेव भूः .. 32 ..
16.255.m: All prosperities are his whose mind is content; / for one whose feet are covered with shoes, is not the earth as if covered in leather? 32.

16.255.s:
saṃtoṣāmṛtatṛptānāṃ yatsukhaṃ śāṃtacetasām..
kutastaddhanalubdhānāṃ sukhaṃ cāśāṃtacetasām ..33..
16.255.d:
संतोषामृततृप्तानां यत्सुखं शांतचेतसाम्..
कुतस्तद्धनलुब्धानां सुखं चाशांतचेतसाम् ..33..
16.255.m: The happiness of those of tranquil mind who are satisfied with the nectar of contentment— / whence could that happiness belong to those greedy for wealth and of untranquil mind? 33.

16.255.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
kāmaṃ kāmayamānasya yadi kāmaḥ sa siddhyati ..
tathainamaparaḥ kāmo bhūyo vidhyati bāṇavat ..34..
16.255.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
कामं कामयमानस्य यदि कामः स सिद्ध्यति ..
तथैनमपरः कामो भूयो विध्यति बाणवत् ..34..
16.255.m: Viśvāmitra said: / If a desire succeeds for one who desires desire, / then another desire pierces him again like an arrow. 34.

16.255.s:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati ..
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivarddhate .. 35 ..
16.255.d:
न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति ..
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्द्धते .. 35 ..
16.255.m: Never is desire extinguished through the enjoyment of desires; / like a fire [fed] with clarified butter, it only blazes up all the more. 35.

16.255.s:
kāmānabhilaṣanlobhānna naraḥ sukhamedhate..
samālabhya tarucchāyāṃ bhavanaṃ vāñcho naraḥ ..36..
16.255.d:
कामानभिलषन्लोभान्न नरः सुखमेधते..
समालभ्य तरुच्छायां भवनं वाञ्छो नरः ..36..
16.255.m: Desiring desires out of greed, a man does not thrive in happiness; / having reached the shade of a tree, a man desires a mansion. 36.

16.255.s:
catuḥsāgarasaṃyuktāṃ yo bhuṃkte pṛthivīmimām ..
ekastu vanavāsī ca sa kṛtārtho na pārthivaḥ ..37.. ..
16.255.d:
चतुःसागरसंयुक्तां यो भुंक्ते पृथिवीमिमाम् ..
एकस्तु वनवासी च स कृतार्थो न पार्थिवः ..37.. ..
16.255.m: The one who lives alone in the forest has fulfilled his purpose, / not the king who enjoys this earth surrounded by four oceans. 37.

16.255.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
pratigrahasamartho yastapo varddhayate mahān..
na karoti tapastasya jāyate ca sahasradhā .. 38 ..
16.255.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थो यस्तपो वर्द्धयते महान्..
न करोति तपस्तस्य जायते च सहस्रधा .. 38 ..
16.255.m: Jamadagni said: / A great one who, though capable of accepting gifts, increases his austerity [instead], / does not [need to perform] austerity: his [merit] is produced a thousandfold. 38.

16.255.s:
pratigrahasamarthānāṃ nivṛttānāṃ pratigrahāt ..
ya eva dadatāṃ lokāsta evāpratigṛhṇatām .. 39 ..
16.255.d:
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थानां निवृत्तानां प्रतिग्रहात् ..
य एव ददतां लोकास्त एवाप्रतिगृह्णताम् .. 39 ..
16.255.m: For those who are capable of accepting gifts but desist from acceptance, / the very same worlds that belong to givers belong to those non-receivers. 39.

16.255.s:
.. aruṃdhatyuvāca .. ..
bisataṃturyathā nityaṃ samaṃtānnālasaṃsthitaḥ ..
tṛṣṇā caivamanādyaṃtā tathā dehāśritā sadā .. 7.1.255.40 ..
16.255.d:
.. अरुंधत्युवाच .. ..
बिसतंतुर्यथा नित्यं समंतान्नालसंस्थितः ..
तृष्णा चैवमनाद्यंता तथा देहाश्रिता सदा .. 7.1.255.40 ..
16.255.m: Arundhatī said: / Just as a lotus fiber remains constantly within the stalk all around, / even so does craving, without beginning or end, ever reside in the body. 40.

16.255.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ ..
yo'sau prāṇāṃtiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham .. .. 41 ..
16.255.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः ..
योऽसौ प्राणांतिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् .. .. 41 ..
16.255.m: Which is hard to abandon for the foolish, which does not age as one ages, / which is a disease that ends only with life—he who abandons that craving has happiness. 41.

16.255.s:
.. caṃḍovāca .. ..
ugrātpratigrahādyasmādbibhyatyete maheśvarāḥ ..
balīyāṃso durbalavattathā caiva bibhemyaham .. 42 ..
16.255.d:
.. चंडोवाच .. ..
उग्रात्प्रतिग्रहाद्यस्माद्बिभ्यत्येते महेश्वराः ..
बलीयांसो दुर्बलवत्तथा चैव बिभेम्यहम् .. 42 ..
16.255.m: Caṇḍa said: / Since these great lords, strong though they are, fear a fierce gift / as if they were weak, so too do I fear it. 42.

16.255.s:
.. paśumukha uvāca .. ..
yadācaraṃti vidvāṃsaḥ sadā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ ..
tadeva viduṣā kāryamātmano hitamicchatā .. 43 ..
16.255.d:
.. पशुमुख उवाच .. ..
यदाचरंति विद्वांसः सदा धर्मपरायणाः ..
तदेव विदुषा कार्यमात्मनो हितमिच्छता .. 43 ..
16.255.m: Paśumukha said: / Whatever the wise who are ever devoted to righteousness practice, / that alone should be done by an intelligent man wishing his own welfare. 43.

16.255.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā hemagarbhāṇi tyaktvā tāni phalāni ca ..
ṛṣayo jagmuranyatra sarva eva dṛḍhavratāḥ .. 44 ..
16.255.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
इत्युक्त्वा हेमगर्भाणि त्यक्त्वा तानि फलानि च ..
ऋषयो जग्मुरन्यत्र सर्व एव दृढव्रताः .. 44 ..
16.255.m: Īśvara said: / Having spoken thus and abandoned those fruits containing gold, / all the seers of firm vows went elsewhere. 44.

16.255.s:
tataste vicaraṃto vai dadṛśuḥ sumahatsaraḥ ..
padminībhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ sarvato varavarṇini .. 45 ..
16.255.d:
ततस्ते विचरंतो वै ददृशुः सुमहत्सरः ..
पद्मिनीभिः समाकीर्णं सर्वतो वरवर्णिनि .. 45 ..
16.255.m: Then, wandering about, they saw a very large lake / crowded on all sides with lotus beds, O fair-complexioned lady. 45.

16.255.s:
tasmindeśe tadā prāptaḥ parivrājaḥ śunomukhaḥ ..
tenaiva sahitāstatra snātāḥ sarve maharṣayaḥ .. 46 ..
16.255.d:
तस्मिन्देशे तदा प्राप्तः परिव्राजः शुनोमुखः ..
तेनैव सहितास्तत्र स्नाताः सर्वे महर्षयः .. 46 ..
16.255.m: At that time, the wandering mendicant Śunomukha arrived in that region; / accompanied by him, all the great seers bathed there. 46.

16.255.s:
tatrāvatāraṃ kṛtvā tairgṛhītāni bisāni tu ..
nikṣipya sarasastīre cakruḥ puṇyāṃ jalakriyām .. 47 ..
16.255.d:
तत्रावतारं कृत्वा तैर्गृहीतानि बिसानि तु ..
निक्षिप्य सरसस्तीरे चक्रुः पुण्यां जलक्रियाम् .. 47 ..
16.255.m: Having stepped down into it, lotus stalks were gathered by them; / placing them on the shore of the lake, they performed the holy water-rite. 47.

16.255.s:
athottīrya jalāttasmātte sametya parasparam ..
bisāni tānyapaśyaṃta idaṃ vacanamabruvan .. 48 ..
16.255.d:
अथोत्तीर्य जलात्तस्मात्ते समेत्य परस्परम् ..
बिसानि तान्यपश्यंत इदं वचनमब्रुवन् .. 48 ..
16.255.m: Then, emerging from that water and assembling together, / not seeing those lotus stalks, they spoke these words: 48.

16.255.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kena kṣudhābhitaptānāmasmākaṃ pāpakarmaṇā ..
bisāni tāni sarvāṇi hṛtāni ca munīśvarāḥ .. .. 49 ..
16.255.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
केन क्षुधाभितप्तानामस्माकं पापकर्मणा ..
बिसानि तानि सर्वाणि हृतानि च मुनीश्वराः .. .. 49 ..
16.255.m: The seers said: / By which evil-doer have all those lotus stalks been stolen / from us who are afflicted with hunger, O lords of sages? 49.

16.255.s:
te śaṃkamānāstvanyonyaṃ paryapṛcchandvijottamāḥ ..
cakruste śapathānsarve yathānyāyaṃ ca bhāmini .. 7.1.255.50 .. ..
16.255.d:
ते शंकमानास्त्वन्योन्यं पर्यपृच्छन्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
चक्रुस्ते शपथान्सर्वे यथान्यायं च भामिनि .. 7.1.255.50 .. ..
16.255.m: Suspecting one another, those best of the twice-born questioned each other; / they all took oaths according to rule, O beautiful lady. 50.

16.255.s:
kaśyapa uvāca .. ..
sarvabhakṣaḥ sa bhavatu nyāsalopaṃ karotu saḥ ..
kūṭasākṣitvamabhyetu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 51 ..
16.255.d:
कश्यप उवाच .. ..
सर्वभक्षः स भवतु न्यासलोपं करोतु सः ..
कूटसाक्षित्वमभ्येतु बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 51 ..
16.255.m: Kaśyapa said: / May he eat anything, may he misappropriate a deposit, / may he incur [the guilt of] false testimony, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 51.

16.255.s:
.. vasiṣṭha uvāca .. ..
anṛtau maithunaṃ yātu para nārīṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
atithiḥ syāttathānyonyaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 52 ..
16.255.d:
.. वसिष्ठ उवाच .. ..
अनृतौ मैथुनं यातु पर नारीं विशेषतः ..
अतिथिः स्यात्तथान्योन्यं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 52 ..
16.255.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / May he engage in sexual intercourse outside the fertile period, especially with another's wife; / may he be an [uninvited] guest of one and all, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 52.

16.255.s:
.. bharadvāja uvāca..
nṛśaṃso vai sa bhavatu samṛddhyā cāpyahaṃkṛ taḥ ..
matsarī piśunaścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 53 ..
16.255.d:
.. भरद्वाज उवाच..
नृशंसो वै स भवतु समृद्ध्या चाप्यहंकृ तः ..
मत्सरी पिशुनश्चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 53 ..
16.255.m: Bharadvāja said: / May he be cruel and arrogant because of prosperity; / may he be envious and slanderous, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 53.

16.255.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
nityaṃ kāmarataḥ sostu divā sevatu maithunam ..
nīcakarmarataścaiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 54 ..
16.255.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
नित्यं कामरतः सोस्तु दिवा सेवतु मैथुनम् ..
नीचकर्मरतश्चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 54 ..
16.255.m: Viśvāmitra said: / May he be constantly addicted to lust, may he engage in sexual intercourse by day, / and may he be devoted to base deeds, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 54.

16.255.s:
.. jamadagniruvāca .. ..
kanyāṃ yacchatu vṛddhāya sa bhūyādvṛṣalīpatiḥ ..
astu vārddhuṣiko nityaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 55 ..
16.255.d:
.. जमदग्निरुवाच .. ..
कन्यां यच्छतु वृद्धाय स भूयाद्वृषलीपतिः ..
अस्तु वार्द्धुषिको नित्यं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 55 ..
16.255.m: Jamadagni said: / May he give a maiden to an old man, may he become the husband of an outcaste woman, / may he constantly be a usurer, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 55.

16.255.s:
.. gautama uvāca .. ..
sa gṛhṇātvavikādānaṃ karotu hayavikrayam ..
prakarotu gurorniṃdāṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 56 ..
16.255.d:
.. गौतम उवाच .. ..
स गृह्णात्वविकादानं करोतु हयविक्रयम् ..
प्रकरोतु गुरोर्निंदां बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 56 ..
16.255.m: Gautama said: / May he accept a gift of sheep, may he engage in selling horses, / may he censure his teacher, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 56.

16.255.s:
(?)atriruvāca .. ..
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ nityaṃ durmatiḥ so'vamanyatām ..
śūdraṃ pṛcchatu dharmārthaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 57 ..
16.255.d:
(?)अत्रिरुवाच .. ..
मातरं पितरं नित्यं दुर्मतिः सोऽवमन्यताम् ..
शूद्रं पृच्छतु धर्मार्थं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः .. 57 ..
16.255.m: Atri said: / May that evil-minded one constantly disrespect mother and father; / may he consult a śūdra on matters of righteousness, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 57.

16.255.s:
.. arundhatyuvāca .. ..
karotu patyuḥ pūrvaṃ sā bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ tathā ..
nārī duṣṭasamācārā bisastainyaṃ karoti yā .. 58 ..
16.255.d:
.. अरुन्धत्युवाच .. ..
करोतु पत्युः पूर्वं सा भोजनं शयनं तथा ..
नारी दुष्टसमाचारा बिसस्तैन्यं करोति या .. 58 ..
16.255.m: Arundhatī said: / May she eat before her husband, and likewise sleep [before him], / a woman of wicked conduct, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 58.

16.255.s:
.. caṇḍovāca .. ..
svāminaḥ pratikūlāstu dharmadveṣaṃ karotu ca ..
sādhudveṣaparā caiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yā ..59..
16.255.d:
.. चण्डोवाच .. ..
स्वामिनः प्रतिकूलास्तु धर्मद्वेषं करोतु च ..
साधुद्वेषपरा चैव बिसस्तैन्यं करोति या ..59..
16.255.m: Caṇḍa said: / May she be contrary to her husband, and may she hate righteousness, / and may she be devoted to hating virtuous people, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 59.

16.255.s:
.. paśumukha uvāca .. ..
parasya preṣyatāṃ yātu sadā janmanijanmani ..
sarvadharma kriyāhīno bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ..7.1.255.60..
16.255.d:
.. पशुमुख उवाच .. ..
परस्य प्रेष्यतां यातु सदा जन्मनिजन्मनि ..
सर्वधर्म क्रियाहीनो बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः..7.1.255.60..
16.255.m: Paśumukha said: / May he fall into servitude to another constantly in birth after birth, / bereft of all rites of righteousness, who commits the theft of the lotus stalks. 60.

16.255.s:
.. śunomukha uvāca.. ..
vedānsa paṭhatu nyāyādgṛhasthaḥ syātpriyātithiḥ ..
satyaṃ vadatu cājasraṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ ..61..
16.255.d:
.. शुनोमुख उवाच.. ..
वेदान्स पठतु न्यायाद्गृहस्थः स्यात्प्रियातिथिः ..
सत्यं वदतु चाजस्रं बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः ..61..
16.255.m:
Śunomukha said:
“May he study the Vedas in accordance with proper rule, be a householder devoted to guests, / and constantly speak truth—he who steals the lotus stalks!”

16.255.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
iṣṭametaddvijātīnāṃ yastvayā śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
tvayā kṛtaṃ bisastainyaṃ sarveṣāṃ naḥ śunomukha ..62..
16.255.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
इष्टमेतद्द्विजातीनां यस्त्वया शपथः कृतः ..
त्वया कृतं बिसस्तैन्यं सर्वेषां नः शुनोमुख ..62..
16.255.m:
The seers said:
“What you have made into an oath is desirable for the twice-born! / By you was the theft of the lotus stalks committed against all of us, O Śunomukha!”

16.255.s:
.. śunomukha uvāca .. ..
mayā hṛtāni sarveṣāṃ bisānīmāni vai dvijāḥ ..
dharmaṃ vai śrotukāmena jānīdhvaṃ māṃ puraṃdaram..63..
16.255.d:
.. शुनोमुख उवाच .. ..
मया हृतानि सर्वेषां बिसानीमानि वै द्विजाः ..
धर्मं वै श्रोतुकामेन जानीध्वं मां पुरंदरम्..63..
16.255.m:
Śunomukha said:
“Indeed, by me were all these lotus stalks taken, O twice-born ones, / wishing to hear of dharma! Know me to be Puraṃdara [Indra]!
”

16.255.s:
alobhādakṣayā lokā jitā vai munisattamāḥ ..
prārthayadhvaṃ varaṃ śubhraṃ sarvameva hyasaṃśayam ..64..
16.255.d:
अलोभादक्षया लोका जिता वै मुनिसत्तमाः ..
प्रार्थयध्वं वरं शुभ्रं सर्वमेव ह्यसंशयम् ..64..
16.255.m: “Through your lack of greed, imperishable worlds have been won, O best of sages! / Request an auspicious boon, everything indeed without doubt!”

16.255.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
ihāgatya naro yastu trirātropoṣitaḥ śuciḥ ..
kṛtvā snānaṃ pitṝṃstarpya śrāddhaṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ ..65..
16.255.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
इहागत्य नरो यस्तु त्रिरात्रोपोषितः शुचिः ..
कृत्वा स्नानं पितॄंस्तर्प्य श्राद्धं कुर्यात्समाहितः ..65..
16.255.m:
The seers said:
“Whatever man, having come here, fasts for three nights, remains pure, / performs his ritual ablution, satisfies the ancestors, and performs a śrāddha with composed mind—

16.255.s:
sarvatīrthodbhavaṃ tasya puṇyaṃ bhūyātpuraṃdara ..
nādhogatimavāpnoti vibudhaissaha modatām ..
tathetyuktvā tataḥ śakrasta traivāntarhito'bhavat..66..
16.255.d:
सर्वतीर्थोद्भवं तस्य पुण्यं भूयात्पुरंदर ..
नाधोगतिमवाप्नोति विबुधैस्सह मोदताम् ..
तथेत्युक्त्वा ततः शक्रस्त त्रैवान्तर्हितोऽभवत्..66..
16.255.m: may the merit arising from all sacred fords be his, O Puraṃdara! / May he not meet a downward path, and may he rejoice with the gods!” / Having said, “So be it,” Śakra then vanished right there.

16.255.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe prathame prabhāsakṣetramāhātmya ṛṣitīrthamāhātmya varṇanaṃ nāma pañcapañcāśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..255..
16.255.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे प्रथमे प्रभासक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य ऋषितीर्थमाहात्म्य वर्णनं नाम पञ्चपञ्चाशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..255..
16.255.m: Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, named ‘Description of the Māhātmya of the Ṛṣitīrtha,’ in the First Prabhāsa-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Seventh Section, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
